label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/snapbug.mdl, models/rip.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, C, D where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a valve wheel, 32 across), the outline is a round rim with six red spokes meeting a diamond-shaped hub on a rust post. Front, back and angled views all show the same ring. The top and side views show a thin ring with the hub block, and no part sticks out or is missing in any view.

M2.reason: Measured size 9 x 31.9 x 34 against the brief's 32 across (sizeOff 0.002), well within 15%.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies: rim, hub, stem, and the spokes it shows in red. The rim is present and steel-coloured at the rim as asked. Six spokes are visible (the bottom one is hidden behind the stem in the front view). The hub's square red collar shows in the left, right and top views. Nothing asked for is missing. The brief sets no number of sides for the rim, so none is charged.

M4.reason: Red paint on the spokes and hub, steel (grey-silver, mottled) on the rim where the paint is worn away, and a rust-brown stem. These match the brief's 'red paint worn to steel at the rim'.

M5.reason: The rim's worn steel with mottled dark spots is clearly visible at the sheet's scale, and the stem has a rust grain. The red spokes are plain, but the brief puts the wear at the rim only, so flat spokes are not a fault.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. Of four readings, judges picked the asset in only one (run 4), so it is not caught twice and does not drop below 2.

M7.reason: The wheel stands upright in the front view, with the hub's spoke at the top and the stem running down to the base. The brief gives no facing, so this is judged on the wheel standing plainly on its stem.

M8.reason: 194 triangles, under the 422 that Half-Life's most-complex prop of its kind uses and about twice the median (99). The below view shows the stem's base closed, and the rim is joined to the hub and stem, so nothing is open or floating.
